senses.gloss:
Dundubhi, apparently an onomatopoetic word, means ‘drum,’ as used in both war and peace. It is often mentioned from the Rigveda onwards. A special sort of drum was the ‘earth drum,’ made by digging a hole in the ground and covering it with a hide. This was employed in the Mahāvrata, a rite performed at the winter solstice, for the purpose of driving away influences hostile to the return of the sun. A ‘drumbeater’ is included in the list of sacrificial victims at the Puruṣamedha or ‘human sacrifice.’
Foot notes i. 28, 5; vi. 47, 29. 31.
Av. v. 20, 1 et seq.; 21, 7; 31, 7; vi. 38, 4; xii. 1, 41; taittirīya brāhmaṇa, i. 3, 6, 2; Śatapatha brāhmaṇa, v. 1, 5, 6; dundubhya, ‘connected with the drum,’ Vājasaneyi Saṃhitā, xvi. 35.
